title: Normal sinus beat

events.label: Sinus node
events.caption: The sinus node, high in the right atrium, fires and starts the beat.
events.ecg: The sinus node is too small to appear on the surface ECG; the trace is still flat.

events.label: Atrial activation
events.caption: The impulse spreads through the right atrial muscle and enters Bachmann's bundle, which carries it across to the left atrium. The atria depolarise together as the P wave.
events.ecg: The P wave is rising: atrial muscle is depolarising.

events.label: AV node
events.caption: The impulse reaches the AV node, the only normal electrical link to the ventricles. It conducts slowly, which makes the pause of the PR segment. The left atrium finishes activating meanwhile.
events.ecg: Near the top of the P wave. The AV node is too small to record, so it leaves no mark of its own.

events.label: His bundle
events.caption: The impulse leaves the AV node and passes through the His bundle.
events.ecg: The trace is flat: the PR segment. The impulse is passing through the AV node and His bundle without a visible signal.

events.label: Bundle branches
events.caption: The His bundle divides into the left and right bundle branches on either side of the septum.
events.ecg: Still on the flat PR segment: the bundle branches are too small to record.

events.label: Purkinje fibres
events.caption: Purkinje fibres carry the impulse quickly over the inner surface of both ventricles.
events.ecg: Still flat, the last moment before the QRS.

events.label: Ventricular activation
events.caption: The ventricular muscle activates: the septum first, from left to right, then the apex and free walls from inside to outside. This is the QRS complex.
events.ecg: The QRS complex begins: the Q wave, then the tall R wave as the large left ventricular mass activates.

events.label: Activation complete
events.caption: The base of the ventricles is the last region to activate. Repolarisation follows.
events.ecg: The QRS ends. A flat ST segment and then the T wave (ventricular repolarisation) follow.

teaching_points: Normal sinus rhythm: the sinus node controls the whole heart, every P wave is followed by a QRS, rate 60 to 100 per minute (slide 9).
The AV node delay produces the PR interval; the Purkinje system makes the QRS narrow.
